Kevin Liu: Hi team — need help. I have custody of my stepson part-time (every other week) and a recent court order updated custody on 2026-02-10. I want to add him to my medical and dental. Does split custody affect eligibility? Also his SSN is pending (application filed). Can I add him now?
Samira Khan: Congrats on getting the order sorted. Short answers: custody arrangements can impact dependent eligibility depending on the carrier, but in most cases a court order granting legal custody/guardianship is sufficient. For split custody we typically need the court order showing you are the custodial parent for benefits purposes or an explicit guardianship clause.
Samira Khan: Docs we need: 1) Court order or custody decree (signed + dated); 2) Proof of the childs identity (passport or birth certificate) — SSN not mandatory at intake; 3) Proof of residence (if required by carrier). If SSN is pending, upload SSA application proof or ITIN application receipt and update later when SSN/ITIN arrives.
BenefitsAdmin: Carriers vary on whether they require the child to be "mainly residing" with you. If the order specifically grants you legal custody for certain purposes (including healthcare), that's usually enough. Please upload the custody order and any supporting docs to the secure portal: https://hr.redwood.com/secure-upload (choose "Dependent Addition (QLE)").
Kevin Liu: The order says "joint legal custody with primary residence to mother" but grants me medical decision rights on alternate weeks. Does that mean I can't add him?
Legal: If the order names primary residence with the other parent, carriers sometimes require a signed consent from the primary parent or a written agreement allowing the non-primary parent to enroll. Best to upload the order and we can escalate to carrier for an exception. Some carriers accept a notarized letter from the other parent consenting to enrollment.
Samira Khan: Exactly. Two options that usually work: (A) get written consent from the other parent to enroll the child on your plan (notarized preferred) OR (B) submit the custody decree and we'll request carrier review — some carriers will accept if you have legal authority for healthcare decisions. We'll start intake with what you have so we don't miss the QLE window.
Kevin Liu: I filed the SSA application this morning but it's pending. I uploaded files: "1814000000_kevin_custody_order.pdf" and "1814000000_ssa_receipt.jpg" to the secure portal. I also emailed the other parent to sign a consent letter, may take a couple days.
People Ops Bot: Reminder: do NOT post PII in channel. Use secure upload: https://hr.redwood.com/secure-upload. Include event date on uploads.
BenefitsAdmin: Got the upload. We'll log this as a QLE dated 2026-02-10 and start carrier intake. We'll request the consent letter if carrier requires it and note SSN pending. Expect an initial response in 2 business days. If the carrier denies due to primary residence, we'll request an exception and document the appeal.
Kevin Liu: Thanks. If carrier denies, can I arrange claims reimbursement for treatment I pay while we appeal?
BenefitsAdmin: You can file claims and we can include a retroactive addition request to the carrier; reimbursement depends on carrier rules. We'll flag urgent claims for expedited review where possible. Keep receipts and provider statements.
Samira Khan: One more note: if carrier requires parental consent and the other parent refuses, we can escalate through Legal to review the decree language for enrolled rights. Upload the consent or refusal correspondence (redact PII) to the portal and we'll advise next steps.
Kevin Liu: Will do. Appreciate the help.
Samira Khan: We'll update this thread once carrier confirms. If anyone else has similar split custody QLEs, please follow the same secure upload flow.
